in_hebrew.name: כריסליה
in_hebrew.meaning: פרח זהב, ניצן זהב במשמעותו הרוחנית
in_hebrew.long_meaning: כריסליה נגזר מהמילה היוונית 'χρυσός' (זהב) ו-'άλια' (פרח או ניצן). במשמעותו הרוחנית, השם מייצג את היופי והערך של הנשמה הנוצרית, כמו גם את ההתפתחות הרוחנית והגדילה בישוע.

in_greek.name: Χρυσάλια
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Χρυσάλια προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις 'χρυσός' (χρυσός, δηλαδή χρυσό) και 'άλια' (פרח או ניצן). Στην πνευματική έννοια, το όνομα αντιπροσωπεύει την πνευματική ανάπτυξη και την ομορφιά της ψυχής του Χριστού.

data.cultural_impact: The name Chrysalia carries a rich cultural significance, rooted in ancient Greek mythology and Christianity. In Greek mythology, the word 'chrysos' refers to gold, a symbol of wealth, power, and prosperity. In the Christian context, this name may evoke images of the golden Tablets of the Testaments, or the golden aureus coins used in the early Christian church as a form of donation. The name may also be associated with the pure gold used in liturgical art, particularly in the construction of altars and icons.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Chrysalia holds profound spiritual significance, highlighting the connection between faith, divine blessings, and the rewards of righteous living. The Greek root 'chrysos' symbolizes the preciousness of gold, and by extension, the worth and value of every human life. The name may also be associated with the biblical passage in Revelation 21:21, which describes the streets of the New Jerusalem as being "pure as gold, clear as crystal." In Christian tradition, this passage is understood as a metaphor for living a virtuous and pure life, worthy of the presence of God. Ultimately, the name Chrysalia serves as a reminder of the beauty and richness of the spiritual life, and the divine blessings that await those who live in accordance with God's will.
